package_scope.excludes: the open PyRosetta-free fallback, the RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN images, and the mosaic, rfdiffusion, bindcraft-open and bindcraft-native batch adapters, all of which belonged to a superseded mixed package

controller_interface.open_dependency: the controller companion must also publish the external tree admission document and point FS2_BINDCRAFT_EXTERNAL_TREES at it, beside .fs2/request.json and .fs2/input-manifest.json; without it the design stage fails closed
controller_interface.mpnn_lane: FS2_BINDCRAFT_MPNN_WEIGHTS selects original or soluble; unset defers to the pinned advanced template. Both colabdesign weight directories are absent from the image and mounted per run.
controller_interface.output_directory: run-trajectory accepts a pre-created empty output directory and rejects a non-empty one rather than merging into a previous attempt
controller_interface.artifact_id_is_not_matched: the admission document's artifact_id must be a non-empty string but is never compared to an expected value; the role key selects the algorithm and mount. The adapter's bindcraft-pyrosetta-installed-tree is preferred over the renderer's example value because it matches the ID in the adapter's artifact-lock.json
controller_interface.input_manifest_digest_is_not_verified: the wrapper cross-checks only request.input_manifest.artifact_id against manifest.manifest_id, so the manifest's own sha256/size_bytes and both files' on-disk formatting are free; request_sha256 is hashed over a re-canonicalization of the parsed request. The target structure itself is still gated: its size and SHA-256 are verified against the manifest entry before design starts. Reported to the adapter task as a deliberate gap rather than silently tightened

reported_defect_in_consumer.finding: shards = min(designs, 32) exceeded accepted_designs_per_shard maximum 10 once designs passed 320, and the schema cannot express more than shard_count 64 x 10 = 640 designs at any shard count, so the adapter's claimed 1..1024 range could not validate

boundaries.641: not representable at any shard count

reported_defect_in_consumer.state: resolved by the adapter task in 8a7a015b
reported_defect_in_consumer.resolution: the adapter refuses above 320 at parse time and names both governing bounds, keeping shards = min(designs, 32) so small requests stay parallel. This is better than the shards = ceil(designs / 10) that was suggested here, which would have collapsed four one-design shards into a single shard doing four designs and serialised work that need not be

open_decision.question: whether BindCraft should be able to run more than 320 designs in one request
open_decision.needs: one of three changes, none of them this task's to make
open_decision.not_taken_here: this task did not raise the cap. parameters.schema.json is not owned by the image task: it arrives on this branch only through the inherited primary-adapters commit and is not yet on main, so its owner is the primary-adapters task, and the public parameter schema that admits 1024 belongs to the scientific runtime onboarding task

options.change: raise the catalog profile's design max_parallelism above 102
raise the native accepted_designs_per_shard cap to at least 16 with 64 shards
lower the public designs maximum from 1024 to 320 so the caller-facing contract stops promising what the platform cannot execute
options.note: proposed by the adapter task as the smallest honest change; narrowing a public contract is its owner's call, and it is recorded here because the first two options were the only ones this record originally listed

open_decision.ownership_verified_by: the adapter task independently, confirming the schema is absent from origin/main, appears on this branch only in the inherited primary-adapters commit, and carries the same change as 47683340 on the primary-adapters branch
open_decision.routed: the runtime-onboarding owner was messaged directly; the primary-adapters task runs as Codex and is unreachable by message, so it received a task-file entry and a table of the three disagreeing bounds in the shared handoff document. Nothing is blocked on either: the adapter fails closed at 320 regardless

provenance_enforcement.why: an attested revision that cannot be resolved back to source proves nothing, which is what r16 shipped
provenance_enforcement.clean_source: publication refuses a dirty working tree across the package and the adapter wrapper
provenance_enforcement.reachable_revision: publication refuses a HEAD not contained in any pushed remote branch
provenance_enforcement.revision_equality: the published SLSA provenance is read back and the attested revision must equal the built revision
provenance_enforcement.context_equality: the attested build context must be this package's path
provenance_enforcement.source_stability: every file that becomes the image is re-hashed after the build and must be unchanged; the fingerprint is recorded and still matches the working tree
provenance_enforcement.adapter_binding: the wrapper is pinned by SHA-256 in the lock, re-hashed by load_lock, and labelled as adapter.wrapper.sha256; the dangling adapter.commit label is gone

stage_topology.handoff: content-addressed: the aggregate re-reads every artifact the design stage published and holds it to that shard's declared SHA-256 and size, rejecting a missing, rewritten or escaping path
stage_topology.server_validated: both current-branch rendered Jobs passed kubectl apply --dry-run=server against k8s-inference-h100; the live design and aggregate then both completed with exit code zero
